cards.title: We grew up doing this for ourselves before we did it for anyone else
cards.text:
THE ORIGIN
RASA started as a small crew throwing 300-person gatherings in living rooms and lofts. We are now a decade on, and we've produced more than 200 events, from members-only salons to 10,000-person festivals in San Francisco, LA, Miami, New York, London, Milan, Dubai, and Paris.
Along the way we built the systems, the team and the technology to run at that scale without losing the intimacy and purpose. Atelier is the service we offer brand leaders asking for the same thing we've mastered and do best: building an incredible room, a talented team, and the tech, built especially for their audience.
Everything we recommend, has been tried and tested on our own real events first. You inherit the optimized playbooks, and we partner with you to dream your biggest dreams, so we can make it happen.

EXPERIENTIAL MARKETING

blocks.t: The Ultimate Guide to Experiential Marketing

blocks.p: Experiential marketing is the discipline of designing live, in-person moments that let people feel a brand instead of just seeing it. Done well, it turns a product story into a memory, a memory into a conversation, and a conversation into measurable growth. This guide covers what experiential marketing is, why it works, the formats brands actually deploy, how to budget for it, how to measure it, and how Atelier by RASA approaches it for Fortune 500 clients.

blocks.t: What is experiential marketing?

blocks.p: Experiential marketing (sometimes called engagement marketing, live marketing, or brand activation) is a strategy where a brand invites its audience into a curated physical or hybrid experience. The goal is not impressions, it is participation. A guest walks in as a stranger and walks out as a fan, an advocate, or a customer with a story to tell.
Unlike a paid ad that interrupts, an experiential moment is chosen. Guests opt in, spend real time inside the brand world, and leave with sensory recall that no banner impression can produce.

blocks.t: Why experiential marketing works

blocks.li: Memory that compounds. Multi-sensory experiences encode more deeply than passive media, which is why guests still describe an activation weeks later.
Earned reach. A well-designed set piece is inherently shareable, turning attendees into a distributed content team.
First-party data. RSVPs, check-ins, on-site interactions, and post-event surveys build a clean opt-in database no third-party cookie can match.
Sales lift. Direct product interaction shortens the path from curiosity to conversion, especially for premium and considered categories.
Cultural credibility. Showing up in the right room with the right people signals that a brand belongs in a scene, not just adjacent to it.

blocks.t: The core formats
Brand activations

blocks.p: Focused, high-intent moments tied to a launch, campaign, or cultural tentpole. Think a product reveal at Art Basel, a suite at Formula One, or a takeover at Fashion Week.

blocks.t: Pop-ups and immersive installations

blocks.p: Temporary environments that let guests walk through a brand narrative, often with an interactive or Instagrammable set piece at the center.

blocks.t: VIP and executive events

blocks.p: Intimate dinners, salons, and private tours designed to deepen relationships with the top one percent of customers, partners, and press.

blocks.t: Conferences and customer summits

blocks.p: Multi-day gatherings that combine content, community, and production value. When festivalized correctly, they become the year's biggest sales moment.

blocks.t: Original festivals and cultural takeovers

blocks.p: Full productions with original creative, ticketed audiences, and multi-stage programming. RASA's THRILL CITY at Six Flags Magic Mountain and Pier Play on the Santa Monica Pier are two examples of this format at scale.

blocks.t: Sponsorships and activation-in-a-box

blocks.p: Showing up inside someone else's audience: a sponsored footprint at a festival, a branded lounge at a conference, or a hospitality program around a live sports moment.

blocks.t: How to plan an experiential activation

blocks.li: Start with the KPI, not the concept. Are you driving trial, loyalty, press, pipeline, or brand affinity? Every design decision follows that answer.
Define the guest. One clear audience beats three fuzzy ones. Cultural fit is the single biggest predictor of whether the room feels alive.
Pick the moment and the venue. The right venue does half the marketing work before the doors open. Iconic destinations turn an event into a story.
Design the narrative arc. Arrival, discovery, peak moment, share moment, exit. Guests should feel the story change as they move through the space.
Engineer shareability. Build at least one hero visual that photographs beautifully and belongs on a feed without a caption.
Wire the tech. RSVP, check-in, guest profiles, upsells, and post-event automation should live on one platform, not five spreadsheets.
Report the ROI. Attribute the outcomes back to the KPI you started with. Anything else is a highlight reel.

blocks.t: Budgets: what experiential marketing actually costs

blocks.p: Costs scale with venue, guest count, production value, and talent. As a working range for brand-side planning:

blocks.li: Targeted activation: roughly $5K to $100K for a focused moment, executed on a proven playbook.
Elevated experience: roughly $100K to $500K for custom creative, richer production, and a larger guest footprint.
Flagship production: $500K and up for original IP, multi-stage programming, and ticketed or invite-only scale.

blocks.p: The real question is not what an event costs, it is what it returns. A $250K activation that closes a seven-figure enterprise deal or unlocks a category conversation is one of the cheapest marketing bets a brand can make.

blocks.t: How to measure experiential ROI

blocks.p: Every RASA program is reported against a small, honest set of metrics:

blocks.li: Attendance and audience quality — verified check-ins, target-account presence, VIP attendance.
Engagement — dwell time, interactions per guest, opt-ins to owned channels.
Earned media — press placements, creator content, organic social reach.
Pipeline and revenue — sourced meetings, opportunities created, closed-won attribution.
Brand lift — pre and post surveys on awareness, consideration, and intent.

blocks.t: Trends shaping experiential marketing right now

blocks.li: Festivalization of B2B. Customer summits are borrowing the production language of music festivals to earn attention.
Owned event technology. Brands are moving off generic ticketing tools onto platforms built for guest experience and first-party data.
Cultural co-signs over celebrity co-signs. The most credible activations partner with communities, scenes, and artists rather than renting a name.
Hybrid capture. Every live moment is designed as a content engine, with post-event edits doing the second wave of marketing work.
Sustainability as a spec, not a slogan. Reusable builds, local sourcing, and measured impact are moving from nice-to-have to procurement requirement.

blocks.t: Common mistakes to avoid

blocks.li: Booking a venue before defining the KPI.
Designing for the founder's taste instead of the guest's.
Confusing headcount with success.
Skipping the tech layer, then losing the data.
Treating the event as the finish line instead of the launch pad.

blocks.t: How Atelier by RASA approaches experiential marketing

blocks.p: RASA designs live brand experiences ranging from targeted activations to fully original productions. Clients inherit the same creative playbook, production expertise, community, and VC-backed technology that powers our own flagship events, from THRILL CITY to Pier Play to Portalverse. We stay accountable for the whole arc: strategy, unparalleled venues, execution, and ROI reporting.
Explore our case studies to see how brands like Google, Rivian, Aston Martin, Delta, ClickUp, and H. Lorenzo have used experiential marketing to move the needle, or learn how Atelier works.

blocks.t: Frequently asked questions
What is the difference between experiential marketing and event marketing?

blocks.p: Event marketing is a category of tactics. Experiential marketing is a design philosophy that can apply to events, retail, sponsorships, or product launches. Every experiential program is an event, but not every event is experiential.

blocks.t: How long does it take to plan a brand activation?

blocks.p: A focused activation can go from brief to doors-open in six to eight weeks. Flagship productions and original IP typically need four to nine months of runway.

blocks.t: How do you measure the ROI of an experiential campaign?

blocks.p: By defining the KPI before the concept and instrumenting the event to report on it: verified attendance, engagement, earned media, pipeline, and brand lift, tied back to the original business goal.

blocks.t: Is experiential marketing worth it for smaller brands?

blocks.p: Yes, when the format matches the budget. A tightly scoped activation for the right 100 guests can outperform a broad campaign that reaches the wrong 100,000.

/press/rolling-stone-rasa-la-to-london.desc: Rolling Stone UK on how RASA expands its experiential reach from LA to London, connecting culture and community in iconic spaces.

blocks.p: ROLLING STONE UK · PRESS FEATURE

blocks.t: RASA Expands Its Experiential Reach: From LA to London, Connecting Culture and Community in Iconic Spaces

blocks.alt: DJ performing to a crowd at RASA's PIER PLAY on the Santa Monica Pier

blocks.p: RASA, an experiential entertainment company based in Los Angeles, has been exploring new approaches to live events by combining art, music, and immersive technology. Known for creating interactive spaces fostering cultural connection and creativity, RASA is building a presence in experiential events that span local and international settings.

Founded by CEO Ahmad Muhaisen, COO Tristan Petit, and CGO Faisal Malas, RASA's leadership team brings expertise in scaling startups, luxury hospitality, and strategic growth, forming a foundation for RASA's growing ambitions abroad.

blocks.t: Developing New Formats in Experiential Events

blocks.p: RASA has organized various large-scale events that blend technology, live performance, and artistic expression, including Thrill City at Six Flags Magic Mountain in spring 2024, which showcased immersive outdoor entertainment. More recently, RASA introduced PIER PLAY, the first Pier Play series event held at the Santa Monica Pier in October 2024. Designed to celebrate art, music, and community, the festival drew a large audience in an iconic LA location, marking a milestone in RASA's evolving event model.

“PIER PLAY is an opportunity to activate iconic spaces like the Santa Monica Pier in a way that connects communities through art and music,” said Ahmad Muhaisen, CEO and Co-Founder of RASA. “Our goal is to create immersive experiences that foster creativity and meaningful connections while respecting the cultural significance of these spaces. With PIER PLAY, we're setting a path forward for how events can create enjoyment and engagement.”
Through events like PIER PLAY, RASA is committed to using public spaces to support local and international artistic expression.

blocks.t: Expanding into New Markets: London and Beyond

blocks.alt: Tim Burton-inspired Jack Skellington installation at Neitherworld with RASA neon sign in London

blocks.p: With its foundation in LA, RASA has extended its reach internationally. Following a collaboration in 2023 with the Mandrake Hotel in London, RASA returned to the UK this past Halloween, partnering with Boneca London to present Neitherworld, a Tim Burton-inspired two-night Halloween event at Exhibition London.

To ensure the event's success, Boneca and RASA teamed up with Exhibition White City, one of West London's leading venues. It is set within a Grade II-listed former Victorian engine house and is located in the vibrant White City district within the Westfield London complex.

Exhibition White City is now gearing up for an exciting new chapter as its partnership with the iconic Flipper's Roller Boogie Palace residency, the legendary 1970s roller rink from West Hollywood once known as the “Studio 54 on wheels,” rolls into its next phase. Exhibition will host events and brand experiences and is launching a cultural programme.

blocks.alt: Laser show at Boneca x RASA Neitherworld event in London with RASA neon sign

blocks.p: This London event reflects RASA's commitment to exploring culturally resonant experiences and collaborating with local partners to engage new communities. Beyond London, RASA has hosted events in cities including San Francisco, Miami, Dubai, Beirut, and Ibiza, supporting its aim to deliver immersive and locally inspired gatherings in cultural hubs worldwide.

blocks.t: Innovative Leadership and a Data-Driven Model

blocks.p: Its founding team's expertise guides RASA's growth and international expansion. CEO Ahmad Muhaisen previously led the growth of fintech startup Tribal Credit, which secured substantial investment, providing him with a strategic approach to scaling innovative ventures. COO Tristan Petit brings experience from luxury hospitality, including his tenure at LVMH, and skills in scaling technology-driven platforms. CGO Faisal Malas, who contributed to the early growth of ClickUp, a fast-growing software company, applies his background in high-growth environments to support RASA's expansion.

“Our tech platform has allowed us to scale efficiently by analyzing data to improve event planning and operations,” noted Faisal Malas, CGO. “It's been instrumental in helping us adapt and deliver unique experiences across different markets.”
By combining data insights, growth strategies, and immersive technology, RASA aims to deliver memorable experiences to audiences in various settings.

blocks.t: Looking Ahead: RASA's Future Expansion

blocks.p: With events like PIER PLAY in LA and the recent Neitherworld in London, RASA plans to expand its event model to new international markets. The company remains focused on blending creativity, community, and immersive technology to engage audiences through unique gatherings.

As RASA builds its presence in the UK and other global markets, it is positioning itself as a company dedicated to creating high-quality, immersive events that extend beyond traditional entertainment. From LA to London and beyond, RASA's approach supports artistic expression and community connection, contributing to the evolving landscape of live events.

/press/la-wire-pier-play-santa-monica-pi.title: LA Wire: PIER PLAY on the Santa Monica Pier | Atelier by RASA
/press/la-wire-pier-play-santa-monica-pi.desc: LA Wire covers PIER PLAY, RASA's experiential festival of sound, creativity, and community on the Santa Monica Pier.

blocks.p: LA WIRE · PRESS FEATURE

blocks.t: PIER PLAY: Where Sunset, Sound, and Culture Collide on the Santa Monica Pier

blocks.s: By Matt Emma, Los Angeles Wire Contributor

blocks.alt: Crowd cheering in front of the Santa Monica Pier ferris wheel at RASA's PIER PLAY

blocks.p: On October 4th, 2025, a golden Saturday in Los Angeles, the Santa Monica Pier—synonymous with California iconography—was reimagined in a new way. As the sun dipped below the horizon, its boardwalk became a cinematic stage for PIER PLAY, an experiential festival of sound, creativity, and community designed by the globally inspired event studio, RASA.

“This is our third event at the Santa Monica Pier in twelve months, and we hope this marks the beginning of our continued collaboration with the Pier and City of Santa Monica,” remarked Ahmad Muhaisen, Co-Founder and CEO of RASA.

Drawing an estimated 3,000 guests from across the world, the event ran from 3:30 PM to 10 PM, blending art, music, and immersive storytelling into what became an unforgettable day-to-night celebration. At its heart was a mission to rekindle the spirit of Los Angeles through global culture, shared experiences, and innovative brand activations.

“We have one of the iconic landmarks in the world as our backyard, and sometimes we take that for granted,” added Muhaisen. “For that reason, we decided to showcase its potential to the world—highlighting it as one of the exciting destinations for people to travel, connect, and rediscover Los Angeles.”

blocks.t: A Global Soundtrack on the Pacific

blocks.alt: PIER PLAY main stage with red lighting and DJs performing at the Santa Monica Pier

blocks.p: The music journey was curated to uplift, connect, and inspire. Featuring Shimza, Nandu, Layla Benitez, Henri Bergmann, Talon, Lubo Hang, and MALAS, the lineup included Afro-house rhythms to melodic techno, painting a soundscape as expansive as the ocean beside it.

As the day transitioned into twilight, the pier pulsed with an energizing atmosphere. The synergy between artists and crowd created an environment that was both cinematic and deeply intimate—hallmarks of RASA's immersive approach.

Central to the musical and aesthetic vision was RASA Co-Founder Faisal Malas, a respected curator and music visionary. His commitment to connecting global artists and crafting emotionally resonant moments made the evening feel carefully curated, if not timeless.

PIER PLAY showcased RASA's signature blend of luxury, artistry, and storytelling—demonstrating Malas's ability to translate creative vision into transformative, real-world experiences that continue to expand RASA's cultural influence.

blocks.t: Brands That Did More Than Show Up

blocks.p: PIER PLAY was more than just a music event—it was a multi-sensory brand playground. Each activation was designed not just to entertain, but to engage meaningfully with guests and align with RASA's mission of purposeful experience.

blocks.alt: Guest playing the -196 Japanese seltzer whack-a-mole activation on the Santa Monica Pier

blocks.p: Beam Suntory, the Japanese beverage powerhouse and main sponsor, curated custom bar experiences with Haku Vodka, Roku Gin, and Maker's Mark. Their -196 Japanese seltzer activation—a nostalgic whack-a-mole game—delighted attendees with branded prizes and became one of the evening's talked-about moments.

Coca-Cola elevated both GA and VIP zones with distinct activations. In GA, guests enjoyed photo booths, tastings, and giant Jenga. The VIP area shimmered with disco balls, neon signage, and custom claw machines, offering exclusive giveaways like sunglasses, bottle openers, and lip balms.
In VIP, Love.com created a lounge that felt like a retreat—infused with positivity, plush décor, and community-driven activations that aligned with RASA's inclusive ethos.

Mac Barber, founder of KYE, brought edge and creativity with on-site haircuts under the pier lights. Nearby, UNDO offered a “spin-the-wheel” hangover prevention activation, while Lunautics had guests shimmering into the night with their glitter and gem glam station.
Dear Caviar added a luxurious touch: complimentary caviar bumps for select guests in the backstage area, reinforcing RASA's love for the unexpected.
And for those looking to move between sets, Huupe's interactive basketball challenge in the GA zone kept things active and competitive, with a chance to win one of their smart backboards.

Perhaps the innovative partnership came from AlphaTheta (formerly Pioneer), which provided select creators with DJ gear in advance, offering tutorials on how to mix and play. This activation empowered self-expression and creativity, and was closely aligned with RASA's mission to democratize artistry.

“All these efforts to bring captivating brands that elevate the experience for our guests are also reflected in our proprietary software,” said Tristan Petit, Co-Founder and COO of RASA. “It allows guests to sign up seamlessly, and for us to better understand who they are—where they come from, what keeps them coming back, and how we can communicate their feedback to our brand partners. It's about shaping a new kind of experience: one that's both playful and purposeful.”

blocks.t: More Than an Event—A Movement

blocks.p: From golden hour to final beat, PIER PLAY embodied everything RASA stands for: community, curation, and culture. It wasn't just another beachside party—it was a global gathering with soul.

RASA is in the process of setting a new standard for live experiences—where brand partnerships aren't just sponsors, but storytellers, where technology supports human connection. And where every guest leaves not just entertained, but inspired.

As they continue to reimagine what's possible at the intersection of artistry and innovation, events like PIER PLAY signal a shift towards a future where every gathering becomes a chance to connect more deeply—with place, with people, and with possibility.

blocks.p: In today's landscape, where audiences yearn for experiences that go beyond the traditional realms of entertainment, RASA's THRILL CITY event at Six Flags Magic Mountain on March 16th, 2024, represents a significant shift. This groundbreaking event combined the pulsating energy of a house music festival with the exhilarating excitement of roller coasters, while also setting a precedent for how entertainment initiatives can substantially contribute to community empowerment and support charitable endeavors.

RASA, established in 2021 by seasoned experts from the tech and entertainment sectors, stands at the forefront of transforming entertainment experiences. This innovative company is dedicated to crafting thematic events that merge electronic music with diverse communities and unique, atmospheric venues. RASA's mission extends beyond traditional event organization; they aim to pioneer event innovation, redefining the entertainment landscape with the seamless integration of their proprietary technology platform. Their events are designed not just to entertain but to foster genuine connections among attendees, promoting positive values and a sense of community.

Today more than ever, Gen Z and Millennials seek deeply engaging experiences that also serve a purpose beyond entertainment. This growing desire for meaningful engagement with entertainment that also facilitates a positive impact on society is at the heart of what RASA achieved with THRILL CITY. By merging electronic music, diverse communities, and unique settings, RASA has tapped into a new wave of audience expectations, offering not only a novel entertainment experience but also a way to contribute to meaningful causes.

The event attracted 4,500 attendees to Six Flags, transforming the park into a vibrant, nocturnal theme park for the first house music festival of its kind at the venue. THRILL CITY featured 22 DJs across three stages and showcased art installations by three innovative artists, all while providing access to some of the park's most iconic roller coasters. This fusion of elements created an immersive experience that elevated the standard amusement park visit into a comprehensive festival atmosphere.

Beyond the music and thrills, THRILL CITY was underscored by a strong commitment to social responsibility. Half of the proceeds from VVIP ticket sales were donated to City Of Hope, highlighting RASA's dedication to supporting cancer research and treatment. This approach reflects a broader trend in entertainment towards integrating philanthropy directly into the fabric of event planning, offering attendees the opportunity to partake in entertainment that not only enriches their own lives but also makes a tangible difference in the world.

RASA's CEO, Ahmad Muhaisen, articulated the company's vision as not merely an entertainment venture but an initiative aimed at harnessing the power of music and community for positive change. “RASA is not just a venture; it's a commitment to using music as a transformative force, creating clean slates that build healthy communities. In this realm, soul and authenticity reign supreme, transcending commerce and hype,” Muhaisen states.

The success and allure of THRILL CITY were further amplified by the involvement of an impressive roster of sponsors, each adding their unique flair to the event. Galpin Motors/Aston Martin, Lo Siento Tequila, Liquid Death, and Feat Clothing not only provided substantial support but also curated unique brand activations that enriched the attendee experience. The Aston Martin VVIP Lounge and the Aston Martini VVIP Bar offered exclusive, sophisticated settings for guests to unwind, reflecting the premium nature of their brands. Meanwhile, Liquid Death quenched thirsts with a twist, promoting sustainability through their canned water, and Feat Clothing showcased their latest fashion lines, adding an element of style to the festival atmosphere. These collaborations highlighted RASA's ability to seamlessly integrate diverse brands into the fabric of THRILL CITY, creating a more engaging and multifaceted event experience.

blocks.p: FLAUNT · PRESS FEATURE

blocks.t: Six Flags Got a Glow-Up, And It’s Called THRILL CITY

blocks.alt: THRILL CITY performer in sequined costume tossing tinsel over the crowd at Six Flags Magic Mountain

blocks.p: For one unforgettable night, Six Flags Magic Mountain shed its teenage skin and transformed into LA’s most exclusive cultural playground, curated not for the masses, but for the tastemakers who shape what’s next.

At the heart of this transformation was RASA, the fast-rising tech and event agency disrupting the live entertainment space with a fresh, genre-defying formula. Their brainchild, THRILL CITY, returned for its second sold-out edition, welcoming thousands inside the gates, and leaving thousands more on the waitlist.

This wasn’t your average festival. It was a multi-sensory takeover, where thrill rides met luxury, and techno met art in a surreal collision of culture. Guests moved through three electrifying stages, each with a distinct energy: The Aurora Loop Stage, powered by Rivian, pulsed with futuristic vibes courtesy of A-Trak, Darius, and DJ Harvey. The Wild Wild RASA Stage, brought to life by Kirgo, radiated heat with bold sets from Birds of Mind to Shimza. At the center, the Thrill Seeker Stage, powered by RASA itself, kept energy sky-high with massive closing sets from WhoMadeWho and Colyn.

blocks.alt: Blue laser fan lighting up the RASA main stage and crowd at THRILL CITY

blocks.p: Scattered across the park were immersive activations and indulgent hideaways: A Veuve Clicquot bar gleamed beside a roller coaster. Bandero and Neft Vodka lounges flanked Tatsu, while a VIP Don Londrés bar served the inner circle. The Plug, a non-alcoholic sanctuary, stood by Maejor’s Vibration Forest, where Rhye opened the night with a transcendent performance.

At the intersection of art and wellness, Secular Sabbath and Biotune curated a calming escape with vibration therapy mattresses, silent disco tech, and poetic interludes from Mia Moretti, a moment of stillness amidst the sensory storm.

Celebrities, creators, and cultural icons roamed freely between coasters and soundscapes, dressed in high fashion and lit by laser beams. Dom Pérignon towers, Rivian ride-ins, and a dreamlike energy elevated the night far beyond traditional nightlife.

But THRILL CITY isn’t just a party. It’s RASA’s masterstroke, a bold proof-of-concept that live experiences can be reengineered into something immersive, intelligent, and unforgettable. They’re not just throwing events. They’re writing a new cultural code, fusing storytelling, tech, and aesthetic mastery to shape the future of IRL connection.

And Six Flags? A legacy giant to see the vision. The partnership didn’t just create a viral moment, it sparked a movement, rewriting a new playbook for where this industry might be headed. THRILL CITY sparked more than a moment. It’s the start of a movement. And the tracks are already laid for where it’s going next.
